control_result.observation: A replay package can be self-checking without being tamper-evident. Internal replay catches mutations only when they break a redundant assertion or an executable relation exercised by the recorded vectors. Provenance-label changes and behaviorally equivalent policy edits can preserve every recorded outcome and therefore cannot be identified as tampering from the mutable record alone.
control_result.inference: For provenance-critical fields, exact replay needs a separate integrity layer. A content hash or Git blob identity can detect changed bytes only when the expected digest/commit identity is obtained from an independently trusted immutable reference; embedding a digest only inside the same rewritable record does not establish originality. A cryptographic signature can bind bytes to a signing key, but authorization, key distribution, rotation/revocation, freshness and canonicalization remain separate unresolved trust questions.
control_result.uncertainty: Not tested: byte-level canonicalization, actual hash/signature computation, signed Git commit verification, repository compromise model, key rotation/revocation/freshness, trust-root distribution, duplicate identifiers, malformed keyid parsing, multiple signatures, threshold policy, heterogeneous verification cost or cross-implementation behavior.
